## LINES

_One moving line._

### Traditional Chinese

#### Scripture

初六：濡其尾，吝。

#### Exegesis

濡其尾，亦不知極也。

### Simplified Chinese

#### Scripture

初六：濡其尾，吝。

#### Exegesis

濡其尾，亦不知极也。

### English, Wilhelm-Baynes

#### Scripture

Six at the beginning means:
He gets his tail in the water.
Humiliating.

#### Exegesis

Six at the beginning:
a) He gets his tail in the water.
Humiliating.
b) “He gets his tail in the water.” For he cannot take the end into view.

### English, James Legge

#### Scripture

1. The first SIX, divided, shows its subject (like a fox) whose tail gets immersed. There will be occasion for regret.

#### Exegesis

1. 'His tail gets immersed:'--this is the very height of ignorance.
